# Client-architecture learnings — consolidated for owner review (2026-07-29)

Compiled from the architecture investigation (exhibits, refactors, repairs). Status: R = ratified by evidence/owner, P = proposed (awaiting decision), C = conflict with an earlier ratified position that must be resolved explicitly. Process-era learnings (monitors, agent drift, canonical values) remain in learnings.md; this file is the client-architecture layer.

| # | Area | Learning | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wiring | The data-widget string registry was right for the framework evaluation (neutrality) and wrong after it: stringly-typed, global scanning, config as serialised JSON, invisible coupling. Retire in favour of imports. | P (C: ADR-004 mandates it) |
| 2 | Wiring | Custom elements give per-instance binding with native lifecycle (connected/disconnectedCallback) and no selectors outside the component — the .astro world's equivalent of a ref. | P |
| 3 | Wiring | The reuse pattern that kills magic: the shared module defines AND registers its element; consumers `import '../scripts/x'` and use the tag. Jump-to-definition works end to end. Real case: kaos-graph (3 consumers). | P |
| 4 | Components | .astro fences accept full Props interfaces — untyped fences were habit, not a language limit. astro check currently reports 152 implicit-any errors across older components. | R (evidence) |
| 5 | Components | .tsx renders statically with zero JS unless given client:*; typed props checked at call site; the only shape that passes config as real values (no JSON-through-attribute hop). Cost: hydration + Preact chunk (~4kB gz shared) when interactive. | R (evidence) |
| 6 | Components | Four component shapes now exist as real files for the hero: string-wired (live), wiring-colocated tsx, fully-inline custom-element .astro, fully-inline tsx. The template bodies are near-identical; the differences are types, wiring, and config transport. | R |
| 7 | Components | Islands are justified by reactive UI state, not performance dogma. Survey qualifies; nav dropdowns/mobile drawer and the form are stronger island candidates than ADR-004's boundary admitted. | P (C: ADR-004 boundary) |
| 8 | Scripts | Zero scripts need global-by-fiat loading. Ownership resolves every case: component-owned (colocate), layout-owned (reveal — imported by BaseLayout's script; legitimate "global" because its owner renders everywhere), shared engines (src/scripts modules). | P |
| 9 | Scripts | public/ is passthrough-only (legacy continuity, fonts, images); first-party behaviour belongs in src/ where the build gives TS, bundling, hashing, per-page loading. Current public/assets/*.js layout is an eval-era artifact. | P (C: ADR-004 placement) |
| 10 | Scripts | Inline vs extract rule: single-use behaviour lives inside its component (either shape); extraction to src/scripts only on ≥2 consumers or excessive size. Promotion is a 5-minute move done when reuse actually happens. | P |
| 11 | Scripts | All first-party behaviour can be TypeScript — colocated `<script>` in .astro is esbuild-processed (TS fine), custom elements and modules type cleanly. Only legacy passthrough (state-of-ml assets) stays .js. | P |
| 12 | Data | A single-consumer data file is displaced page content (projects.json: one consumer, whole homepage §03 materialises from an unreferenced file). Rule: data files earn existence with ≥2 consumers or genuine tabularity; otherwise content belongs in the page's front matter, passed as explicit props. | P (C: ADR-005 "shared or tabular" was applied too loosely) |
| 13 | Data | Facts that appear in multiple places (repo stars) must be single-sourced or they diverge — same trap as the r7 canonical-values finding, now applied to metrics. A refresh script per fact-source beats hand-editing. | R (recurring evidence) |
| 14 | Data | YAML works for data: Astro data collections (glob/file loaders) accept YAML with Zod schemas — typed, loud-failure data instead of silently-imported JSON. Also answers "does it need src/data at all": collections are the idiomatic home; the folder is a choice, the schema is the point. | P |
| 15 | Quality | The gates never measured code readability — line-golfed TSX (476-char lines) and over-formatted output (one attribute per line) both passed. A formatting floor (Prettier/ESLint) plus astro check belongs in the verify gates. | P |
| 16 | CSS | Markup↔CSS contract drift caused a class of layout regressions; the .home-section contract fixed section rhythm structurally. The same discipline question now applies to component CSS: central sheets vs scoped styles is due for reassessment during the CSS cleanup (scoped styles were deliberately rejected in ADR-003 when the design system was ported as shared sheets). | P (C: ADR-003) |
| 17 | Hardcoding | Owner-editable content keeps leaking into components under pressure (mission lines in Hero, §03 copy in projects.json, footer line). The countermeasure is structural review (content-free components as a PR criterion), not one-off fixes. | R (recurring) |
| 18 | Astro features | Unused-but-relevant: astro check as a gate, prefetch, RSS (@astrojs/rss for the newsletter), view transitions, astro:env (forms endpoint), pagination (future lists), content-layer loaders (future members registry), MDX element mapping (future prose treatments). SSR-class features permanently excluded by GH Pages. | R (inventory) |

## Conflicts requiring explicit resolution (the ADR amendment scope)
- ADR-004: data-widget registry + public/ placement + vanilla-only boundary → superseded by #1-3, #7-11 if ratified.
- ADR-005 + conventions: src/data/ JSON guidance → tightened by #12-14 (consumer rule, YAML/collections, refresh scripts).
- ADR-003: central-sheets-only CSS → reopened by #16 for the CSS cleanup phase.
- learnings.md "no npm deps without ADR note" era instinct vs adopting @astrojs/rss, yaml loader etc. → each addition still gets its ADR note; the instinct survives, the blanket avoidance does not.
